name: Animal empathy
check_raw: [[Animal]]s and dire animals have a [[difficulty class]] of 15 + the creature's [[hit dice]]. For [[beast]]s and [[magical beast]]s, the DC is 19 + the creature's hit dice. If the check succeeds, the creature is [[dominated]].
use_raw: Select this skill (from the [[quickbar]]) and then select the target creature. Dominated creatures will be commanded as if they were henchmen. The creature will remain dominated for one [[turn]] per [[character level|level]] of the character using the skill.
special_raw: If the character fails their check by five or more, the creature will go hostile.
description: A successful check allows a character to charm or dominate certain creatures.

name: Appraise
check_raw: The character makes an opposed roll against the [[merchant]]'s appraise skill. If the merchant wins, the character pays more for the goods in the store. If the character wins, he pays less. The first time the player interacts with a merchant dictates the prices in that store until his appraise skill improves.
use_raw: Automatic in stores
description: The higher the [[character]]'s [[skill]], the better the price received when selling or purchasing goods.

name: Bluff
check_raw: The more difficult the con, the more difficult the check
use_raw: Selected in dialog
description: The character can make the outrageous or the untrue seem plausible. The skill encompasses acting, conning, fast talking, misdirection and misleading body language.

name: Concentration
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] to avoid casting failure is equal to 10 + damage received + spell level.
use_raw: automatic
description: Concentration checks are made whenever a character is distracted during the act of casting a spell. It is also used to avoid the effects of the [[taunt]] skill.

name: Craft armor
classes_raw: [[arcane archer]], [[assassin]], [[barbarian]], [[bard]], [[blackguard]], [[champion of Torm]], [[cleric]], [[druid]], [[dwarven defender]], [[fighter]], [[Harper scout]], [[monk]], [[paladin]], [[pale master]], [[ranger]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[rogue]], [[shifter]], [[sorcerer]], [[wizard]]
check_raw: Based on the difficulty to craft this particular item (see in-game crafting menu)
use_raw: Use crafting component
description: The character knows how to create most types of armor, shields, and helmets from different materials.

name: Craft trap
classes_raw: [[arcane archer]], [[assassin]], [[barbarian]], [[bard]], [[blackguard]], [[champion of Torm]], [[cleric]], [[druid]], [[dwarven defender]], [[fighter]], [[Harper scout]], [[monk]], [[paladin]], [[pale master]], [[ranger]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[rogue]], [[shifter]], [[sorcerer]], [[wizard]]
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is determined by the type of trap being created. The more powerful the trap, the more difficult it is to build and the more components it requires.
use_raw: selected
description: The character using this skill can combine raw components to form various [[trap]] kits. There is a 10% chance on any failed skill roll that the components are lost, even though a trap was not crafted.

name: Craft weapon
classes_raw: [[arcane archer]], [[assassin]], [[barbarian]], [[bard]], [[blackguard]], [[champion of Torm]], [[cleric]], [[druid]], [[dwarven defender]], [[fighter]], [[Harper scout]], [[monk]], [[paladin]], [[pale master]], [[ranger]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[rogue]], [[shifter]], [[sorcerer]], [[wizard]]
check_raw: Based on the difficulty to craft this particular item (see in-game crafting menu)
use_raw: Use crafting component
description: The character knows how to create most types of weapons and ammunition from different materials.

name: Disable trap
check_raw: There are four progressively difficult actions that a character may perform on a trap; the base [[difficulty class|DC]] is determined by the difficulty rating of the trap and is modified by the action being performed. Assessing a trap to determine its difficulty modifies the DC by -7. Flagging a trap to make it visible to the rest of the party modifies the DC by -5. Disarming a trap uses the base DC. Recovering a trap modifies the DC by +10.
use_raw: Assess, flag, recover, and disarm are radial menu options off of a detected trap.
special_raw: [[Rogue]] is the only class capable of disarming traps with a DC of 35 or greater. With 5 or more ranks in the [[set trap]] skill a character gets a +2 [[synergy bonus]] on disable trap checks.
description: This skill allows the character to perform a variety of actions on a [[trap]].

extra_labels.spectacular failure: When disarming or recovering a trap, a spectacular failure results in the trap immediately going off if a DC check is failed by 10 or more.

name: Discipline
classes_raw: [[barbarian]], [[bard]], [[blackguard]], [[champion of Torm]], [[dwarven defender]], [[fighter]], [[Harper scout]], [[monk]], [[paladin]], [[ranger]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[weapon master]]
check_raw: The [[DC]] is equal to the attacker's [[attack roll]].
use_raw: automatic
description: A successful check allows the character to resist any combat feat ([[disarm]], [[called shot]], [[knockdown]], or [[sap]]).

name: Heal (skill)
check_raw: To heal poisons and diseases, the healer must make a successful [[skill check|check]] against their [[difficulty class]]. If he is successful, the target is healed and is cured a number of [[hit point]]s equal to the skill roll, plus all modifiers. If the target suffers from no poisons or diseases, it is still cured of damage.
use_raw: Use healing kit on wounded creature.
description: With this skill a character can use a [[healer's kit]] to cure wounds and heal [[poison]]s and [[disease]]s.

name: Hide
check_raw: The character must succeed at an opposed test against a searching creature's [[spot]] check. Success means that the character goes undetected.
use_raw: Select the stealth action from the Special Abilities [[radial menu|radial]]. Opposed spot and [[listen]] rolls are made once per [[round]], where applicable.
special_raw: The hide and [[move silently]] skills combine into a single [[stealth]] action. Movement in stealth mode is slower than the normal rate. [[Armor check penalty|Wearing armor]] or using a [[torch]] inhibits this ability, but low light can provide a bonus. A character in stealth mode is harder to spot if standing still, and if his [[small stature|stature is small]].
description: This skill allows a character to hide from enemies.

name: Intimidate
check_raw: The character can use this skill to change others' behavior with a successful check.
use_raw: Selected in dialog
description: The character can use this skill to get a bully to back down or make a prisoner give him the information he wants.

name: Listen
classes_raw: [[arcane archer]], [[assassin]], [[barbarian]], [[bard]], [[dwarven defender]], [[harper scout]], [[monk]], [[pale master]], [[ranger]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[rogue]], [[shadowdancer]], [[shifter]], [[weapon master]]
check_raw: Listen detects hidden creatures by opposing their [[move silently]] check. A successful check renders the hidden creature visible, and makes it a valid target for the listener.
use_raw: Listen is part of the [[detect]] modal action. In passive detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active detect mode is a modal action that reduces the normal movement rate and makes the character perform an active listen, as well as [[spot]] and [[search]] checks.
special_raw: Standing still provides a +5 bonus to a listen check. A character with the [[alertness]] feat gains a +2 bonus on listen checks. [[Ranger]]s gain a bonus when listening against a [[favored enemy]]. [[Elf|Elves]], [[gnome]]s, and [[halfling]]s gain a +2 racial bonus to listen checks. [[Half-elf|Half-elves]] receive a +1 racial bonus.
description: '''Listen''' alerts a character to hidden creatures that may be nearby.

name: Lore
check_raw: A roll against an unidentified item's value to determine magical properties that the item may possess.
use_raw: Automatic every time the player inspects an item.
special_raw: [[Bard]]s are able to identify items easier than other classes. Various spells and items can also give a character a bonus to their lore skill.
description: '''Lore''' allows a character to identify unknown magic items.

name: Move silently
check_raw: A move silently check is opposed by the listening creature's [[listen]] check. If the character is successful, the opposing creature remains unaware as the character moves.
use_raw: Select the Stealth action from the Special Abilities radial. Invisible creatures automatically enter stealth mode.
special_raw: [[Hide]] and move silently are combined into a single modal [[stealth]] action. Movement in stealth mode is slower than the normal rate. Wearing armor may incur a [[armor check penalty|penalty]], but low-light can provide a bonus.
description: A character may sneak quietly past an enemy.

name: Open lock
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is determined by the lock's difficulty rating. A successful check opens the lock.
use_raw: Select the skill and then target a locked object.
special_raw: [[Thieves' tools]] can be used to provide bonuses to a character's open lock attempt, but are destroyed in the attempt whether successful or not.
description: The '''open lock''' skill allows the character to enter locked rooms and open locked containers.

name: Parry
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is the modified attack roll of the incoming blow. A successful parry means that the attack does not damage the parrying character. A character may only parry a number of attacks per round equal to the number of attacks per round available to the character.
use_raw: Select the parry mode. The character will remain in parry mode until the mode is exited.
special_raw: Wearing armor may incur a [[armor check penalty|penalty]] to the roll. If the parry is successful and the difference between the roll and the DC is ten points or greater, a counterattack occurs. A counterattack is a free attack made by the parrying character, at his full attack bonus, against the parried opponent.
description: '''Parry''' allows the character to block incoming attacks and make spectacular counterattacks.

name: Perform
check_raw: None required. The higher the [[skill point|rank]] in this skill, the better the bard song.
use_raw: Select the skill and it will affect a 30-foot radius of allies around the singer.
description: A [[bard]] using '''perform''' can perform the [[bard song]], which improves their allies' ability to fight in combat and withstand mind-affecting enemies. Perform is essential for any bard who wants to have access to their bard song.
conflict_note: requires training: label says false, Category:Skills that require training says true

name: Persuade
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is determined by the NPC being spoken to.
use_raw: Used in conversation.
description: A successful '''persuade''' check prompts [[non-player character|NPCs]] to reveal additional information or give bonus treasure in conversation.

name: Pick pocket
check_raw: There are two parts to successfully picking a pocket. First the item must be acquired, and then the targeted creature must not notice the theft. Stealing the item is a simple [[skill check|skill test]] against the target's [[difficulty class]]. The base DC for a neutral or tolerant creature is 20, and 30 for a hostile creature. This roll is modified by [[armor check penalty|armor check penalties]]. The targeted creature then makes an [[opposed check|opposed]] [[spot]] check against the character's pick pocket check. Hostile creatures have a +10 bonus to their spot checks in this test. If the targeted creature succeeds at this opposed check, then the target has detected the theft attempt. An [[non-player character|NPC]] who detects the attempt will turn hostile, and a [[player character|PC]] will be informed that the character has attempted to use pick pocket on him. If the character is successful at both checks, then he steals the item without being detected.
use_raw: Select skill, then select valid target.
description: '''Pick pocket''' allows a character to remove items from another's backpack.

name: Ride
description: The character has spent time training to use a horse in combat, and can perform actions unskilled people cannot.

extra_labels.note: Horses and the ride skill are only used in the [[premium module]] "Neverwinter Nights - Wyvern Crown of Cormyr" and specific community-made modules.

name: Search
check_raw: Detecting a trap is an opposed test, pitting the character's search check against a [[difficulty class]] equal to the [[set trap]] skill check, plus the strength of the trap. Only rogues may detect traps with a DC greater than 35.
use_raw: Search is part of the [[detect]] modal action. In passive detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active detect mode is a modal action that reduces the character's normal movement rate and performs an active search, as well as [[spot]] and [[listen]] checks.
special_raw: [[Elf|Elves]] and [[dwarf|dwarves]] receive a +2 bonus to their search checks and [[half-elf|half-elves]] gain a +1 bonus.
description: Search is used to detect traps, find hidden objects, and secret doors.

name: Set trap
check_raw: When a trap kit is used, the character makes a skill check. The [[difficulty class]] of the task is determined by the power of the trap.
use_raw: Use a trap kit from your inventory. An icon visible to you and your party will appear on the ground to represent the trap.
special_raw: Having 5 or more [[skill point|rank]]s in the [[disable trap]] skill grants a +2 [[synergy bonus]] on set trap checks. Any party members will be able to see traps that the character has set.
description: This skill allows a character to place [[trap]] kits.

extra_labels.spectacular failure: If a skill check is failed by 10 or more, the trap goes off in the attempt to set it. This can only occur if you are in combat when trying to set the trap.

name: Spellcraft
check_raw: A successful check means that your character has identified a spell being cast by an opponent. The [[difficulty class]] of this check is equal to 15 + [[spell level]]. The character also gains a +1 bonus for every 5 [[rank]]s in this skill to all [[saving throw]]s against spells.
use_raw: Spellcraft checks are automatic whenever a spell is cast nearby.
special_raw: A specialist wizard gets a +2 bonus when dealing with a spell from his specialized [[spell school|school]]. As well, a successful spellcraft check is required before your character can attempt to counterspell. The specialist wizard suffers a -5 penalty when dealing with a spell or effect from a prohibited school.
description: '''Spellcraft''' is used to identify [[spell]]s and to perform [[counterspell]].

name: Spot
classes_raw: [[arcane archer]], [[assassin]], [[champion of Torm]], [[dwarven defender]], [[red dragon disciple]], [[shadowdancer]], [[ranger]], [[rogue]], [[shifter]], [[weapon master]]
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is determined by the [[hide]] check of the hidden creature.
use_raw: Spot is part of the [[detect]] modal action. In passive detect mode, checks are made automatically every round. Active detect mode in a modal action reduces the normal movement rate and makes the character perform an active spot, as well as [[search]] and [[listen]] checks.
special_raw: The [[alertness]] feat grants a +2 bonus on spot checks. [[Ranger]]s receive a bonus on spot checks against their [[favored enemy]]. [[Elf|Elves]] gain a +2 bonus on spot checks, and [[half-elf|half-elves]] gain a +1 bonus.
description: A successful '''spot''' check reveals a hidden creature.

name: Taunt
check_raw: The [[difficulty class]] is a [[concentration]] check made by the target against the character's taunt skill roll. It is considered an attack. If the taunt is successful, the opponent suffers an [[armor class]] [[dodge bonus|penalty]] equal to the difference between the Taunt roll and the defender's roll (to a max of a -6 penalty) for 5 [[round]]s. The target will also suffer a 30% chance of [[spell failure]], if they don't resist the taunt.
use_raw: Select skill and then target creature.
description: '''Taunt''' is used to provoke an enemy into dropping his guard for a short time.

name: Tumble
check_raw: DC 15 to avoid attack of opportunity while moving.
use_raw: Automatic
special_raw: Wearing armor may incur a [[armor check penalty|penalty]] to the roll.
description: Characters with high tumbling skill are able to roll away from attacks during combat, positioning themselves safely at all times. Anytime the character might receive an [[attack of opportunity]] for moving past enemies, they will automatically attempt a Tumble check against a [[difficulty class]] of 15. If successful the attack is avoided. For every 5 [[rank]]s in this skill (base ranks only, not including feat-, [[dexterity]]- or [[item]]-bonuses) the character's [[armor class]] is also improved by +1.

name: Use magic device
check_raw: The base [[difficulty class]] (DC) of this task is determined by the value of the item, and modified by the type of emulation the character is attempting. If the character attempts to emulate a specific race, the DC increases by 5; if he attempts to emulate a specific alignment, the DC increases by 10. Emulating a specific class does not modify the base DC. You must make a DC check of 25 + the [[innate level|level]] of the spell to cast a spell from a [[scroll]] if the [[difficulty setting|difficulty mode]] of the game is set to Hardcore or higher.
use_raw: Automatically applied whenever a character attempts to use or equip an item normally unusable by his class, race, or alignment.
description: A successful '''use magic device''' check allows a [[character]] to use a magic item as if your character had the required [[class]], [[race]], or [[alignment]].
